stories.title: PM statement on October 7th attacks
stories.summary: Three years after the 7 October attacks in Israel, Prime Minister Andy Burnham remembered those killed, condemned antisemitism and pledged support for Jewish communities, including protection for synagogues, schools and community buildings. He reaffirmed support for a two-state solution.

stories.title: 🤖 Tech / AI / Digital — Government backs recommendations of NHS doctors-led AI Commission
stories.summary: Published 6 October: ministers accepted all 44 recommendations on healthcare-AI regulation. The MHRA opened AI Airlock Phase 3, focused on post-market monitoring, while an implementation roadmap is due by spring 2027.

stories.title: 🏗️ Procurement signal — UK takes next step towards first digitally native government bond
stories.summary: Published 6 October: HM Treasury appointed six joint lead managers after a competitive procurement for the DIGIT pilot. The planned Q1 2027 pilot will test distributed-ledger technology in sovereign bond issuance.

stories.title: 💰 Spending / VfM — Government buys time on shared services (background; 5 Oct)
stories.summary: Background commentary, not fresh news: TechMarketView analysis published 5 October (outside the 24-hour news window) says the government accepted the Public Accounts Committee’s recommendations but deferred most substantive answers until an independent review due in April 2027. The commentary flags unresolved value-for-money, governance and delivery questions.

stories.title: 🤝 Private sector / Consulting — DWP takes Universal Credit review work back in-house (background; 5 Oct)
stories.summary: Background commentary, not fresh news: TechMarketView analysis published 5 October (outside the 24-hour news window) says DWP is bringing 2,700 Teleperformance staff on the Universal Credit targeted case review programme in-house. The article describes this as a change of operating model rather than a performance failure, with the programme extended to 2031.

stories.title: First Speaker's Apprenticeship Academy graduates complete programme with 100% employment success
stories.summary: The House of Commons reported on 6 October that the inaugural two-year Speaker's Apprenticeship Academy cohort completed its programme; all apprentices secured employment or a further career opportunity.

stories.title: Labour figures rule out working with Greens after ‘Zionism is racism’ vote
stories.summary: Senior Labour figures said cooperation with the Greens was unlikely after the party adopted a motion treating Zionism as racism. The report also notes internal pressure on Labour to rule out a future arrangement and Lib Dem criticism of their existing Southwark coalition with the Greens.

stories.title: Badenoch denies plan for ‘British Iron Dome’ – after Tories use phrase in press release
stories.summary: At the Conservative conference, Kemi Badenoch distanced the party’s proposed “Britannia Shield” from Israel’s Iron Dome after the phrase appeared in a press release. The Guardian reports the party proposed £1bn a year for the system, and that Badenoch rejected a post-election deal with Reform in favour of another election.

stories.title: Ed Davey attacks Badenoch conference pledges as unfunded
stories.summary: In a 6 October report on Kemi Badenoch’s conference speech, Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey called the Conservatives’ promises unfunded and said his party would hold them accountable and oppose handing Nigel Farage the keys to No. 10.

stories.title: Reform MP raises concerns about second homes – then buys one for £800,000
stories.summary: The Guardian reported on 6 October that Sarah Pochin bought an £800,000 Anglesey home two days after asking the housing minister about second-home effects on rural housing. The article says the purchase was made jointly with her husband and that they retain another home in Cheshire.

stories.title: SNP pressed for detailed plans after dropping disability law
stories.summary: Published 6 October: a cross-party group of 12 MSPs and charities urged Scottish ministers to set out concrete measures after abandoning the planned Learning Disabilities, Autism and Neurodivergence Bill. Minister Maree Todd said the government would pursue policy and service reforms, citing £7.6m for children’s neurodevelopmental support, while keeping future legislation open.

stories.title: Overseas territories representation proposal raises possibility of seats in the Lords
stories.summary: At a Conservative conference fringe event on 6 October, Lord Ashcroft backed potential legal action over the Chagos deal; Sky News also reported a document from the Conservative Friends of the Overseas Territories suggesting territorial representatives could take seats in the House of Lords.
